did.unittitle: Milbank Memorial Fund records

physdesc.extent: 36 letter-size document boxes; 2 legal-size document boxes; 1 (4x6) card file box; 1 (18x14) flat document box; 1 records carton.

accessrestrict.head: Conditions Governing Access
accessrestrict.p: Open for research with select materials restricted as noted. The Milbank Memorial Fund's deposit agreement stipulates a restriction period of 20 years from the date of creation for records pertaining to the Board of Directors and related Committees and a 10-year restriction for records relating to the development and administration of the Fund's programs and projects.
RAC provides an access surrogate of digital media and born-digital files, not the original files. To request an access surrogate be made, please contact a RAC archivist.
When requesting audiovisual material, please check the "Access" note for each Title. If a Title does not currently have an access copy, please contact a RAC archivist for further instruction.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: The Milbank Memorial Fund signed a deposit agreement with the Rockefeller Archive Center on January 29, 2025, which governs the deposit and use of its records.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Original order, as received, with some minimal arrangement. Files have been grouped into 8 series to facilitate access:

1. Board of Directors and Committees 2. Projects 3. Reforming States Group (RSG) 4. President's Office and Correspondence 5. Policy and Program 6. Milbank Memorial Fund History and Centennial 7. Published Reports and Books 8. Photographs and Audiovisual Material

userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: The Milbank Memorial Fund retains legal title, copyright, and literary property rights in the records.
The RAC has authority to give permission to publish and cite materials from this collection. The RAC will refer to the Depositor requests for permission to reproduce material in its entirety.

relatedmaterial.head: Related Materials
relatedmaterial.p: The main collection of Milbank Memorial Fund records, from 1898-1977 (with additions to 2000) is held by Yale University Library, Manuscripts and Archives, MS 845.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Milbank Memorial Fund records particularly document the Fund's work from the late 1980s to 2014. Records consist of Board Meeting agendas and Committee reports; Project records and reports; the Reforming States Group's meetings, governance, and related correspondence; memos on Policy and Program and the Fund's direction; and reviews and reflections on the Fund's history and accomplishments.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: The Milbank Memorial Fund is an independent operating foundation that works to improve population health and health equity through its dissemination of evidence-based research and its support for and collaboration with state policy leaders and decision makers.

The Milbank Memorial Fund was established in 1905 by Elizabeth Milbank Anderson as a general-purpose charitable foundation in memory of her parents. First known as the Memorial Fund Association, the foundation was renamed the Milbank Memorial Fund upon Anderson's death in 1921, at which time it had an endowment of $10 million. The Fund's early work focused on disease prevention and health care delivery, including, in the 1920s, three demonstration projects in urban and rural areas of New York State.

The Fund's programs evolved as new problems or new solutions were identified. Milbank programs addressed population health and demography, nutrition, housing and hygiene, chronic diseases and epidemiology, mental health services, medical education, and preventive and community medicine, among other issues.

In the 1960s-1970s, the Fund supported fellowships, education, and training in medicine, public health, and the social sciences in the U.S., Latin America, and Africa. But the Fund has consistently viewed research as the critical underpinning of informed health policy.

Daniel Fox's appointment to the presidency in 1989 marked a return to the Fund's more traditional focus on health policy. The Fund undertook a series of policy reviews in the early 1990s and worked to promote the use of systematic reviews of clinical evidence as a basis for informed policy decisions. Around the same time, the Fund played an instrumental role in the creation and establishment of the Reforming States Group, whose bipartisan meetings provided state leaders and policymakers with an opportunity to share information, experience, and practical strategies for health policy reform.

The Fund also aids health policymakers and practitioners through its publication program. Through the Milbank Quarterly, a peer-reviewed journal it launched in 1923, books published in the Milbank "Health and the Public" series with the University of California Press, and its general Milbank Reports, the Fund disseminates the results of research it has supported.

The Directors' Board Books also contain Committee reports. Separate Publications Committee records were not retained in this series as they are fully represented in the Board Books.

did.unittitle: Projects

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Projects series documents the studies, meetings, reviews, and publications that the Milbank Memorial Fund supported and/or initiated from 1990-2009. Project files include information on the project's approval and its relation to the Fund's broader program, correspondence, meeting records, progress reports, and often a final product or report. For the most part, the project files are arranged as received.

Reforming States Group (RSG)

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Reforming States Group (RSG) was the name adopted by a group of state legislators and policymakers who began meeting in the early 1990s to share information and discuss issues and practical strategies for healthcare reform. The Milbank Memorial Fund underwrote the costs of these meetings and helped to organize the initial meetings. The RSG operated from 1992–2021 as a bipartisan group that provided peer-to-peer education, collegiality, and leadership, enabling Federal and State collaboration in policy reform.

The RSG records consist of project and meeting records, plus records of the RSG Steering Committee, which planned and organized the group's program and regional meetings. The collection also includes a file of testimonial letters, solicited on the RSG's tenth anniversary. There are also photo files from several of the Steering Committee meetings.

did.unittitle: Published Reports and Books

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Series 7 contains various "Milbank Reports," published in the 1990s -2000s, and twenty-seven books, most published by the University of California Press in partnership with the Milbank Memorial Fund.

The Milbank Reports publicized findings and discussions that emerged from Fund-supported projects and helped make the information available to policymakers. Reports were often published in collaboration with other organizations. In addition to the reports in this series, several project files also include the Milbank reports pertaining to their research.
The reports and books in this collection have been listed either individually or in the notes, and they should be searchable by title.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series consists primarily of portrait photos of Milbank Memorial Fund officers. There are also two general files of Portraits and Photographs, mainly containing historic photos of people, events, and projects associated with the Fund, and a few additional portraits. Other files concern the illustration or design of the Fund's Centennial Report. There are also a few general Milbank Memorial Fund photo files that require further identification.
The series includes a video of H. Jack Geiger, M.D., Out in the Rural, concerning his Mississippi Health Center project.
A video record of the Fund's Centennial Dinner is filed with other materials on the celebration in Series 6.
